preconditions: filename is null or points to a readable null-terminated byte string.
A non-empty filename must fit in the recovered 256-byte local destination; the raw copy has no bound.
The fallback registry count and 132-byte-stride entries are readable if direct open fails.
postconditions: Null or empty filename returns 0 before file access.
Failure to open directly or through all registry entries logs through content_bootstrap_r2_runtime_leaves.packet_002.v1 and returns -2.
A header matching the 410 literal enters allocation, initialization, parse-result dispatch, optional list insertion, and optional output assignment.
Parse results -2 and -1 release a non-null allocated object through the forwarding and free dependencies and return that value.
Parse result 0 appends the recovered object pointer to the list rooted at 0x008B8F14, increments 0x008B6AC0, and returns 0; if output is non-null it receives the recovered object pointer.
Headers matching the 400 or 401 literals log an incorrect-file message and return -1; other headers return 0.
side_effects: Copies and path-prepares a local filename, opens a direct or prefixed path, reads 12 bytes, and closes the handle through compiler-runtime wrappers.
On the 410 path allocates 308 bytes and invokes the promoted initializer and parser contracts.
On parse failure invokes the promoted forwarding stub and compiler-runtime free wrapper for a non-null object.
On parse result 0 mutates the list head or tail link at offset 0x130, writes the new object's back link at 0x12C when appending to a non-empty list, and increments the global count.
Writes the recovered object pointer through output on the 410 path when output is non-null.

external_dependencies.name: compiler-runtime path preparation, file I/O, string comparison/formatting, allocation, and free wrappers

unresolved: The concrete type and total layout of the 308-byte allocation are unknown.

The recovered root body renders the parser call as sub_55FC40(SrcStr), while the promoted parser contract is thiscall-shaped with an object context plus filename; how the object context reaches that callee is not established by this static C rendering.
Allocation failure still reaches the recovered parser call, and a zero parse result may attempt to register a null object; actual behavior is not established.
Parser return values outside -2, -1, and 0 leave the local result at 0 and may expose or leak the allocation; the reachable return domain is unknown.
The 12-byte read result is unchecked and the local header buffer's termination before strcmp is not established.
Filename capacity, registry bounds, list integrity, synchronization, and eventual teardown ownership are unknown.
The stdcall signature and pointer-shaped integer types are raw decompiler evidence and have not reached ABI_REVIEWED.
tests_required: Unit: null/empty input, direct open, ordered prefix retry, and total-open-failure paths.
Unit: exact 410/400/401/other header dispatch and error codes.
Unit: -2, -1, 0, and unexpected parser return paths, including allocation failure.
Unit: empty and non-empty list insertion, back/next links, count update, and output assignment.
Negative: bound the local filename copy, validate short reads and header termination, and protect list mutation before implementation.
Integration: resolve the parser this-context mismatch and later object teardown before code generation.
